questions.q: What did Trump's advisers try to get him to understand about South Korea?
a: A good relationship with it mattered while North Korea tested weapons
It should pay the entire cost of the US military presence there
It was no longer a useful ally for American trade interests
It had secretly been selling missile technology to North Korea
questions.why: Lesson 1 says at least three advisers made the case for maintaining the alliance.

questions.q: How did Trump react to Gary Cohn's data supporting free trade?
a: He refused to examine any of the evidence
He accepted it and dropped his tariff plans
He asked for a second report by outside economists
He used the data to renegotiate NAFTA quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Cohn had reams of data printed out, and Trump would not look at it.

questions.q: What does Trump call his Twitter account?
a: His megaphone for speaking to the public unfiltered
His window into what the media really thinks
His shield against unfair press coverage
His private diary for close advisers only
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he uses the word megaphone to describe how he reaches people directly.

questions.q: What did Trump's team conclude the most popular tweets had in common?
a: They relied on shock
They included policy details
They were posted late at night
They avoided personal attacks
questions.why: Lesson 3 says he had high-performing tweets analyzed and found shock was the key.

questions.q: What did Trump tell a colleague real power comes from?
a: Never backing down, staying strong and always pushing forward
Building consensus and admitting mistakes early
Delegating decisions to experienced advisers
Keeping a low profile until the results are clear
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls this part of a philosophy of never apologizing or showing weakness.
